This may be caused by bash-language-server's hardcoded `--external-sources` flag triggering unbounded ShellCheck memory growth. We hit the same pattern — 73 concurrent shellcheck processes consuming 17.8 GB, with individual processes growing to 3-5 GB RSS.

The upstream root cause fix has been merged: [bash-lsp/bash-language-server#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376) adds a `shellcheckExternalSources` config option. Setting it to `false` omits `--external-sources` entirely.

**Immediate workaround** — set this env var before running opencode:
```bash
SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false
```

Once opencode bumps its bash-language-server dependency to include this change, the config will be available natively. See also #16269 for the full analysis and #16271 for the `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP` mitigation PR.

The RAM consumption you're seeing (+17 GB just from starting opencode) is likely caused by bash-language-server's hardcoded `--external-sources` flag triggering unbounded ShellCheck memory growth. We observed the exact same pattern — individual shellcheck processes growing to 3-5 GB RSS, compounding across sessions.

The upstream root cause fix has been merged: [bash-lsp/bash-language-server#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376) adds a `shellcheckExternalSources` config option. Setting it to `false` omits `--external-sources` entirely.

**Immediate workaround** — set this env var before running opencode:
```bash
SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false
```

See #16269 for the full analysis. The git/rustc CPU issues you mention may be separate problems, but the RAM explosion is very likely this.

Update: the per-session memory multiplication is significantly worse when bash-language-server's hardcoded `--external-sources` flag triggers unbounded ShellCheck memory growth. Each session spawns its own bash-language-server, each of which spawns its own shellcheck processes that grow to 3-5 GB RSS.

The upstream root cause fix has been merged: [bash-lsp/bash-language-server#1376](https://github.com/bash-lsp/bash-language-server/pull/1376) adds `shellcheckExternalSources: false` to omit `--external-sources`.

This doesn't solve the architectural issue of per-session LSP duplication, but it eliminates the worst memory offender. Setting `SHELLCHECK_EXTERNAL_SOURCES=false` before running opencode is an immediate workaround.

Respectfully, we decided to provide the description of everything that was going on to a language model and then allow it to write the request issue post. We did this because our word choice is inferior to the choices that can be made by a language model, which refines what we think into mannerisms that are more understandable for a human.

Whilst we don't understand why there is a requirement not to have AI-assisted content, it seems quite unnecessary for us to rewrite it. It was originally our own words, and it was simply bolstered by the help of a language model.

We will not be rewriting this, but there does seem to be an issue with the selected model change for some reason. There are other bugs that are similar, so we still believe it was flagged incorrectly.

The description was, in fact, AI-assisted, but it is just for readability purposes because our writing tends not to be the greatest.

Thank you.

I’m seeing a broader local MCP failure on Windows desktop OpenCode that looks related to existing stdio/handshake issues, but not identical to either:

#12229 — local stdio MCP handshake timeout with npx
#6994 — Windows local MCP with bun fails, but npx works
In my case, the problem is wider:

local stdio MCPs fail not only with bun, but also with:
npx
bare command names from PATH
.cmd wrappers
direct node.exe <dist/index.js>
the same MCP servers run fine when started manually outside OpenCode
OpenCode can read config successfully, but the MCP runtime layer is unstable:
/config works
/mcp either returns MCP error -32000: Connection closed
or hangs / times out entirely
This affects both existing built-in/local MCP entries and newly configured local MCPs.

Environment
OS: Windows 11
Client: OpenCode Desktop
OpenCode runtime observed: opencode-cli.exe serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <random_port>
Transport affected: local stdio MCP
Transport not clearly affected the same way: some remote MCPs can connect, but many remote/default MCPs also cause startup slowness or hanging
Affected local MCPs
Examples I tested:

filesystem
fetch
sequential-thinking
git-local
context7
puppeteer
github
What I verified
1) OpenCode sees the MCP config
OpenCode local API /config returns the configured MCP entries correctly.

I verified both:

global config
project-level config
So this is not just “config file not loaded”.

2) Manual execution works
Running the MCP servers directly on Windows works fine.

Examples:

node.exe .../@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem/dist/index.js <paths>
node.exe .../@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking/dist/index.js
node.exe .../@cyanheads/git-mcp-server/dist/index.js
node.exe .../@modelcontextprotocol/server-github/dist/index.js
Observed behavior:

process stays alive
server reports it is running on stdio
no immediate crash / no immediate exit
So this is not a broken package install.

3) OpenCode MCP runtime fails
Inside OpenCode, the same local MCPs fail.

Observed patterns:

sometimes /mcp returns entries like:
status: failed
error: MCP error -32000: Connection closed
after restart / on some instances:
/mcp itself hangs and times out
/config still works while /mcp is stuck
4) Explicit connect does not fix it
I also tried explicit connect calls through the local OpenCode API:

POST /mcp/{name}/connect
These returned 200 true, but the MCPs still ended up as failed / closed afterward.

5) This is not Bun-specific
Unlike #6994, this is not resolved by switching away from Bun.

I tested multiple local command styles and the failure persists:

bun family not required to reproduce
npx still fails
direct node.exe + dist/index.js still fails when launched by OpenCode
Reproduction pattern
Configure one or more local stdio MCP servers in OpenCode on Windows
Start or restart OpenCode Desktop
OpenCode loads the config (/config confirms this)
Local MCPs do not become usable
Depending on the instance:
they show Connection closed
or /mcp hangs / times out
Expected behavior
Local stdio MCPs should connect and remain available in OpenCode, especially when:

the same exact command works manually
the process stays alive outside OpenCode
config is clearly loaded by OpenCode
Actual behavior
OpenCode loads the config
local stdio MCPs still fail internally
OpenCode may become very slow
MCP runtime status endpoint may hang
local MCPs are effectively unavailable
Why this seems different from existing issues
Similar to #12229
local stdio MCPs fail inside OpenCode
manual execution works
suggests a handshake / runtime integration issue
Similar to #6994
Windows-specific symptoms
can produce MCP error -32000: Connection closed
Different from both
failure is not limited to Bun
switching command style does not help
even direct node.exe <dist/index.js> launched by OpenCode still fails
issue seems broader than a single wrapper/runtime problem
OpenCode local MCP subsystem may become unstable enough that /mcp itself hangs

Hey, thanks for the implementation attempt.

Would this work for us?

Well, to be honest: No.

I only just realized this now, but if I understand correctly, you also want the small_model to be used for the explore agent. We don’t want that. We just want to be able to configure a model per provider but keep the existing small_model behavior, i.e. _only_ session title generation.

In my opinion, the use cases of explore agent and session title generation are too different to bunched together into a single config. The models we intend to use for title generation are very fast and capable of doing good summarisation, but they are not necessarily good at tool calling. They would not be fit for usage with the explore agent.

Also, this creates confusion about the semantics of small_model. The global one is only for session title generation, the per-provider one is also used for the explore agent. This is bad design that will definitely lead to misunderstandings.

The PR (and also this issue, as I’m realizing now) seem to mix up these concerns. I think the chances of it getting merged like this are pretty low.

I would suggest to handle things separately:

- one issue / PR for specifying small_model per provider, without changing the semantics of small_model (our use case).
- one issue / PR for providing a _separate_ way to control the model of the explore agent per provider (your use case). Maybe this could even be approached from a completely different direction: It does not only apply to the explore agent, it applies to all agents. You could think of things like
  - move this from the provider config to the agent config: instead of just allowing a single model to be configured with an agent, make it possible to configure a model per provider for the agent
  - alternatively, allow providing a „priority list“ of models to be used with the agent, which would be compared against the models available in the current provider

Something like that…


Aside from that, the basic small_model per provider implementation you have done is similar to what I have also tried out locally. There are some details to decide, e.g. whether the provider name should be required with a `/` for the per-provider small_model. You allow with and without, but just checking for `/` in the model name may not be robust since model names might contain slashes further back in their name. A better approach would be to check if it starts with `<provider>/`. And there are arguments for and against having the provider name in there. Not 100 % what the best approach is.

One more thing: I would recommend to remove the `model` from the example in you original issue description. It seems like you don’t actually want that and it just causes confusion regarding what this issue is about.
